hotspots.title: Dashboard
hotspots.summary: The panel across the front of the cabin that holds the instruments, vents and controls.
hotspots.detail: The dashboard also hides the heating and ventilation unit, wiring and the passenger airbag. Its layout aims to keep frequently used controls within easy reach.

hotspots.title: Steering wheel
hotspots.summary: Turns the front wheels through the steering column and rack.
hotspots.detail: Modern steering is usually power assisted by an electric motor, which reduces effort at low speed. The wheel also houses the driver airbag and common controls.

hotspots.title: Centre display
hotspots.summary: A touchscreen for navigation, media, phone and vehicle settings.
hotspots.detail: Good display design keeps essential functions reachable with minimal glances, and many functions can also be controlled by voice or steering-wheel buttons.

hotspots.title: Centre console
hotspots.summary: The raised unit between the front seats with the gear selector and storage.
hotspots.detail: Consoles commonly include cup holders, a charging tray, an armrest bin and the drive-mode or gear selector.

hotspots.title: Front seats
hotspots.summary: Adjustable seats for the driver and front passenger.
hotspots.detail: Seat adjustment lets drivers of different sizes reach the pedals and wheel comfortably. Head restraints help limit neck injury in rear impacts.

hotspots.title: Rear seats
hotspots.summary: A three-person bench that can fold to extend the cargo area.
hotspots.detail: Split-folding backrests let you carry long items while keeping one or two rear seats available.

hotspots.title: Glove box
hotspots.summary: A lidded storage compartment in front of the passenger.
hotspots.detail: Despite its name it is mostly used for documents, the owner's manual and small items.

hotspots.title: Cargo area
hotspots.summary: The luggage space behind the rear seats, reached through the tailgate.
hotspots.detail: A low, flat loading floor and a wide tailgate opening make heavy items easier to load.

hotspots.title: Front airbags
hotspots.summary: Airbags in the steering wheel and dashboard that inflate in a serious frontal impact.
hotspots.detail: Crash sensors trigger an inflator within milliseconds. The airbag cushions the occupant and then deflates. Airbags supplement seat belts; they do not replace them.

hotspots.title: Curtain airbags
hotspots.summary: Airbags along the roof rails that cover the side windows in a side impact or rollover.
hotspots.detail: Curtain airbags help protect occupants' heads in both rows of seats.

hotspots.title: Seat belts
hotspots.summary: Three-point belts that restrain occupants during sudden deceleration.
hotspots.detail: Pretensioners tighten the belt at the start of a crash and load limiters let it give slightly to reduce chest forces. Seat belts are the most important occupant safety feature.

hotspots.title: Front crumple zone
hotspots.summary: Structure at the front designed to deform and absorb crash energy.
hotspots.detail: By crushing progressively, the front structure lengthens the time over which the vehicle slows, lowering the forces on the occupants inside the stiffer cabin.

hotspots.title: Rear crumple zone
hotspots.summary: Energy-absorbing structure behind the cargo area.
hotspots.detail: The rear structure absorbs energy in rear impacts and helps keep the cabin intact.

hotspots.title: Stability control
hotspots.summary: Uses wheel-speed and motion sensors to brake individual wheels if the car starts to skid.
hotspots.detail: Electronic stability control compares where the driver is steering with where the vehicle is actually heading and briefly brakes selected wheels to help keep it on course.

hotspots.title: Front radar sensor
hotspots.summary: Measures the distance and speed of vehicles ahead for driver-assistance features.
hotspots.detail: Radar works in rain and darkness and supports functions such as adaptive cruise control and automatic emergency braking.

hotspots.title: Windshield camera
hotspots.summary: A forward-facing camera that recognises lane markings, signs and obstacles.
hotspots.detail: Camera and radar data are often combined (sensor fusion) for more reliable driver assistance.

hotspots.title: Parking sensors
hotspots.summary: Ultrasonic sensors in the bumpers that detect nearby obstacles when parking.
hotspots.detail: They emit high-frequency sound pulses and time the echoes, warning the driver with tones as the distance shrinks.
